newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME lean hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent per lb higher while pork belly futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent higher, livestock analysts said.

Further strength in hog futures is expected following steady to higher cash hog indications and expectations of reduced hog marketings the next couple of months. Hog marketings have became current and seasonal supplies tighten going into the summer, analysts said.
Although pork cutout values were down, product prices were expected to firm soon, they said.

Carryover demand is also seen in pork bellies despite weakness in cash product as the continued light pace of slaughter, tight storage stocks and technicals provide underlying support. Expectations of another out-movement from storage last week compared to in-movements last year is also expected to lend support, they said.

Analyst estimates on the weekly CME out-of-town storage report ranged from out 250,000 to 500,000 lbs. This compares with an out-movement of 366,000 lbs last week and an in-movement of 202,000 lbs last year.
